newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court upholds Florida redistricting plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court upholds Florida redistricting plan.

text.p: The Supreme Court Wednesday narrowly upheld as constitutional a redistricting plan for the Florida state senate.

The high court by 5-4 rejected arguments by private attorney C. Martin Lawyer charging that one of the districts in the Tampa Bay area was unconstitutional because the boundaries had been drawn along racial lines.

After mediation, all of the parties except Lawyer reached an agreement in which the boundary lines would be modified so blacks would make up about 40 percent of the district's population, down 10 percent from the initial proposal.
Lawyer objected on the grounds that the boundaries still reflected an unconstitutional racial motivation.

A three-judge federal court upheld the plan, saying it "passes any pertinent test of constitutionality and fairness." It said the district "offers to any candidate, without regard to race, the opportunity to seek elective office."

The majority opinion by Justice David Souter for the Supreme Court upheld the lower-court decision. "In short, the evidence amply supports the trial court's views that race did not predominate over Florida's traditional districting principles in drawing (the boundaries)," Souter concluded.
